role: a computational / regulatory-genomics researcher analyzing labeled DNA sequences
subject: a DNA nucleotide sequence (fixed length, alphabet A/C/G/T)
property: a binary label associated with each sequence (task 'H3' = a histone-mark / chromatin-occupancy classification benchmark)
request: Each row is a 500-base-pair DNA nucleotide sequence (alphabet A/C/G/T) with a binary label (0/1) and a task identifier; every row here belongs to the 'H3' task -- a histone-modification / chromatin-occupancy classification benchmark in which label 1 marks sequences whose genomic region is positive for the H3 histone mark and label 0 marks negatives. Find a concrete, novel, testable question these labeled sequences can answer, decide your own method, run real code on the sequences, and produce a short publishable paper.

data.schema: DNA_CSV (dna.csv): 10000 rows x 3 columns. 'sequence' = a DNA string of 500 nucleotides over the alphabet {A,C,G,T}; 'label' = binary class (int 0 or 1); 'task' = benchmark task identifier (string; all rows = 'H3').
data.summary:
DATASET: labeled DNA sequences for a histone-mark classification benchmark ('H3' task).
  n_items = 10000 rows, each an independent example (no train/test split column is provided here).
  sequence: fixed length = 500 bp (min=500, max=500), alphabet strictly {A,C,G,T}.
  label: binary; COMPUTED balance from the real data -> {"1": 5145, "0": 4855} (roughly balanced).
  task: all rows = {"H3": 10000} (single-task file).
  INTERPRETATION: task 'H3' is a chromatin/epigenetic classification benchmark; a positive label means the sequence's genomic region carries the H3 histone mark, a negative label means it does not. The only signal available is the raw nucleotide sequence itself.
